content.confidence_and_caveats:
- **High confidence**: identity, current CNRS-researcher status at IRAP/OMP Toulouse, ORCID 0000-0001-8130-9832, contact email, and SPEARHEAD-HE project parameters (ID 101135044, dates, total cost, IRAP partnership). All backed by official CNRS, CORDIS, and SPEARHEAD channels.
- **Medium confidence**: the EGU25-12787 paper names Nénon as a co-author at IRAP for the Saturn plasma model within ESA's TRAPPED framework — strong signal of active research alignment but not itself proof of a competitive grant award in his name. No public budget, grant ID, or his formal role within ESA TRAPPED was retrievable.
- **Lower confidence / no public evidence**: any ANR grant naming Nénon as PI, any specific 2026 PhD or postdoc posting with him named as supervisor, any public LinkedIn profile or recent LinkedIn post by him. Searches of EURAXESS France, ANR, CNES TOSCA, and IRAP's job pages did not surface such evidence.
- **Self-correction / anti-confirmation**: I deliberately checked for namesakes (Quentin Pelletier, Quentin Lalanne, Quentin Scott, etc.) and rejected any match lacking IRAP/CNRS Toulouse nexus. I also rejected the "OMP" Greenhouse job board as a misroute to a logistics vendor rather than Observatoire Midi-Pyrénées.
content.synthesis_how_the_pieces_fit: Comparing the three dimensions (identity, funding, hiring) for Q. Nénon against a "standard competitive-grant PI" pattern reveals divergence: he has rock-solid institutional identity and sits on a multi-million-euro EU consortium (SPEARHEAD) and the ESA TRAPPED framework, yet no public record names him as the personally-awarded PI of an ANR, ERC, or CNES competitive grant under his own name since 2024-01-01. Implications: outreach should be anchored on his institutional lab (IRAP/OMP) and group (PEPS / space-plasma teams) rather than on a personal grant database hit; hiring interest should monitor the IRAP `formation-emploi/theses` channel and SDU2E doctoral-school listings more closely than EURAXESS. The CTAO/IRAP PhD posting is gamma-ray astronomy, not planetary plasma — function-adjacent but not in his domain.
